intro: The lake's own boating rules in brief, and where to find fuel and a pump-out.

items.note: Sunrise to sunset on weekends and holidays, from the Saturday before Memorial Day to Labor Day. The regulation sets no numeric daytime limit on weekdays or outside that season.
So says the Fish and Boat Commission's page for the lake.

items.n: Within 100 feet of shore, docks and people
items.note: The statewide rule: slow, no-wake speed within 100 feet of the shoreline, docks, launch ramps, swimmers, downed skiers, people wading, anchored, moored or drifting boats, floats, and anywhere so marked. The button above draws that 100-foot strip along the shore.
From the bridge to a point about 1,000 feet downstream.
From the dam to a point about 600 feet south.
Between the island and the Pike County shore.
Not allowed on weekends and holidays between a buoyed line about 200 yards east of Cairns Island and the Ledgedale Recreation Area.
Not allowed anywhere on the lake on weekends and holidays.

sections.title: Fuel on the water
sections.text: Only marinas that say on their own websites that they have a gas dock are listed. Others may sell fuel: call ahead, and expect docks to close for the winter.

items.note: The Fish and Boat Commission says sewage pump-out is available here for a fee.

sections.title: Depth
sections.text: The Fish and Boat Commission gives the lake as about 60 feet at its deepest. No openly licensed depth survey of the lake was found, so this map shows no depth contours.

fine: A summary, not the regulations and not a chart. Buoys and posted signs on the water come first, and rules change.
